what_it_does: Millimeter-wave communication (5G, satellite) needs a local oscillator signal—a pure reference clock with almost no noise or spurious tones. Traditional voltage-controlled oscillators at mm-wave frequencies struggle with phase noise (random timing jitter). Harmonic-extraction approaches require power-hungry amplifiers. This work proposes a quasi-class-E Colpitts oscillator, a circuit topology that combines a transformer-based resonator to generate clean fundamental oscillation, waveform shaping for efficiency, and integrated noise suppression. The result: -124.9 to -119.8 dBc/Hz phase noise at 10MHz offset—among the best for mm-wave.
